text.p: Lehman Brothers raised its 1997 earnings per share (EPS) estimate for Israel's Elscint Ltd but retained its neutral rating of three in a report released on Thursday.
Analyst Ted Kundtz cited stable gross margins and the impact of a cost-containment programme as his reasons for boosting 1997 EPS to $0.55 from an earlier estimate of $0.40.

He said revenues for the maker of medical-imaging equipment were on track while gross margins showed an improvement in the fourth quarter. As a result, fourth-quarter EPS was $0.09 a share, compared with his $0.05 estimate.
"While there continues to be considerable pricing pressure throughout the diagnostic medical-imaging industry, Elscint should nonetheless show improvement in earnings in 1997," Kundtz said.

He said Elscint's recently announced plan to form a joint venture in nuclear medicine with GE Medical Systems would save research and development costs. "The joint venture should be solidly profitable from the outset," he added.
